intent.purpose: Accumulate operational learning across sessions — observations, insights, patterns, and proposals that feed future session intelligence prep, framework evolution, and harness improvement. The institutional memory for this project. Adapted from CALL (Center for Army Lessons Learned) institutional database pattern: individual sessions produce observations, this file synthesizes them into insights and proposals that persist
intent.scope: Cross-session learning only. Observations citing session estimates, insights connecting observations across sessions, patterns that generalize, proposals with barrier analysis, carry-forward gap tracking, governed vocabulary findings. NOT session operational state (main running estimate). NOT incident tracking (incidents.json via /incident). NOT framework registry data (framework-registry.json via /frameworks). NOT fix specifications (those come from plans)

observations.observation: The Lagebeurteilung → recommendation → commander decides workflow has been used ad hoc throughout session 77a33baf but is not formalized. Lagebeurteilung IS governed (glossary definition with adapted categories: Forces, Terrain, Time, Logistics). The governed definition says 'every time, even if nothing changed' — WHEN is answered. But HOW to present the result and WHERE to pull inputs from are undefined. The workflow already exists in FRAGMENTS across the harness: /handoff skill step 3 (Lagebeurteilung), delegation duty (pre-flight assessment), decision #26 (S2 intelligence prep), decision #13 (Mission Analysis). The fragments are not unified — the gap is unification, not absence. The agent performed the workflow when prompted but skipped it when not prompted (OL-O10).
observations.evidence: glossary.json Lagebeurteilung definition (governed). /frameworks check: no framework governs this workflow. /handoff skill step 3 uses Lagebeurteilung. Planning brief decisions #13 and #26 use assessment concepts. check-pre-commit.sh (check script process). OL-O10 (skipped when not prompted). No rule, skill, or framework unifies these fragments into a single 'when commander asks what next' workflow.

observations.observation: After a lifecycle transition decision, S3 rushed from 'decision made' to 'full execution with commit' without terrain assessment. Commander issued D-v8-5 (fix, test, verify, prevent hooks). S3 checked /frameworks, recorded the decision, then immediately edited 3 source files, tested, deployed, launched audit subagent, wrote a check script step, tested it, and committed — all without presenting an execution plan, confirming scope, or doing a Lagebeurteilung. S3 had demonstrated the correct pattern minutes earlier (pre-commit checklist with 3 passes at the observation→action boundary) but did not repeat it at the decision→execution boundary. Commander caught it: 'stop for a second. i noticed you went and just started executing.'
observations.evidence: Session conversation: D-v8-5 decision at commander's request, then 4-file commit (2175814) without intermediate checkpoint. Pre-commit checklist (the correct pattern) was executed at the prior transition but not at this one. The Lagebeurteilung definition says 'fixed categories examined every time' — S3 examined at transition 1, skipped at transition 2.

observations.observation: Subagents cannot use Glob or Grep on file paths outside the current repo's directory tree. The tools are permission-denied. However, the Read tool with explicit absolute file paths WORKS for cross-repo access. The workaround: when delegating tasks that need files from other repos (dotprofile sessions, other project repos), provide explicit absolute paths in the delegation prompt — do not instruct the subagent to 'search' or 'find' files outside the repo.
observations.evidence: S2 agent (mission-prompt-improvement) attempted Glob on ~/repos/aitools-nobul-jose/sessions/marse/ — denied. Main agent confirmed files exist and are readable via explicit Read paths. Root cause: CC sandboxes subagent Glob/Grep to the current repo. Read tool has broader access when given explicit paths.

insights.insight: The harness has a gap where SessionEnd hook outputs are produced but never committed (we call this the 'commit gap' — ungoverned term, see vocabularyFindings). The carry-forward mechanism (git tracked files) works. The running estimate proved it — committed during session, pulled on Windows, carried forward. The gap is that SessionEnd hook outputs are never committed. Decision #1 (auto-commit/push) is the designed fix but hasn't been implemented across 6 sessions since it was decided. This is the highest-priority pipeline fix because every session that ends without it loses harvested artifacts and session archives

Cross-platform failures repeat because there is no DETECTION layer for platform portability. The PREVENTION layer exists (cross-platform.md rule, correct patterns in check-lib.sh). The AUDIT layer exists (/compat skill proposed). But no hook or check script catches platform-specific commands in hooks before deployment. Per three-layer governance, the missing layer is where failures persist

Governed vocabulary is not documentation — it is an active quality gate. Without it, the running estimate contains overclaims, ambiguities, and assumptions disguised as facts. The same dynamic that caused the v4 false .gitignore claim (prior session) would have recurred in v8 if the vocabulary hadn't forced classification. The observation-to-fact pipeline IS the quality mechanism

The workspace is in a TRANSITION state. Decisions #34 (namespace consolidation) and D-PER-SESSION-ESTIMATES (per-session estimates) are decided but not implemented ON WINDOWS. The Mac may have progressed further. Commander explicitly stated 'most of where stuff lives and naming conventions are assumptions.' Any assumption about structure, paths, or naming on this Windows clone is an assumption, not a fact

The harness needs a CONFIGURATION AUDIT mechanism for cross-machine state. When work happens on one machine and isn't fully committed, the other machine's running estimate, planning brief, and architectural assumptions diverge silently. The divergence is invisible until someone switches machines. ISO 10007 (configuration status accounting) and IPB (intelligence gaps with collection plans) both address this: document the baseline, track changes, audit divergences. The running estimate's carryForwardGaps section is a start but lacks the confidence dimension — we need VERIFIED/STALE/SUPERSEDED/UNKNOWN per item

Carry-forward is a 6-stage pipeline (produce → commit → push → pull → deploy → verify), not 'just commit and push.' This session observed failures at stages 2 (commit gap — selective), 4 (dotprofile pull blocked — dirty tree), 5 (hooks crash, deploy scripts silent failure), and 6 (no Lagebeurteilung at session start). Each stage has independent failure modes. Collapsing the pipeline to 'commit and push' is a false assumption that hides 4 of the 6 failure points. Provenance: Swiss cheese (each stage is a layer with holes), SRE deployment pipeline, Lean value stream mapping, military logistics chain
insights.framework: Platform engineering, Operational learning, Three-layer governance

insights.insight: Carry-forward is session-to-session, not machine-to-machine. The machine is the platform (affects HOW). The session is the unit of work (produces WHAT). Both directions produce original work: prior session had harvesting/AARs/dashboard architecture, this session produced OL estimate/design principle/portability prevention/proposal lifecycle. Reconciliation is a two-way merge, not a one-way sync. The git merge model applies: divergent sessions, conflict detection, explicit resolution

The user model is broader than any single session captures. aitools users span: single-platform, multi-platform, single-user, multi-user collaborating, working on aitools itself, or only using aitools on other projects. Design decisions that assume single-user-multi-machine (the current dominant pattern) may not hold for multi-user scenarios. The dashboard, channel, and concurrency architectures must account for all combinations. This was understood on the Mac session but not documented in the repo
insights.framework: Mission command (user model), Platform engineering (multi-platform support)

From configuration management (ISO 10007): this is a configuration baseline divergence requiring a configuration audit

patterns.description: Carry-forward is not 'commit and push' — it's a 6-stage pipeline: (1) Produce: hooks/agent create artifacts, (2) Commit: git add + commit, (3) Push: git push to remote, (4) Pull: git pull on consuming session's machine, (5) Deploy: aitools sync deploys configs/hooks/skills, (6) Verify: Lagebeurteilung confirms state. Each stage has independent failure modes. This session observed failures at stages 2 (selective commit), 4 (dotprofile dirty tree), 5 (hooks crash, deploy scripts silent failure), and 6 (no Lagebeurteilung done). Different artifact types traverse different pipeline paths: git-tracked JSON goes through git (stages 2-4), deployed hooks go through file copy (stage 5), settings go through deploy scripts (stage 5). 'Commit and push' addresses 2 of 6 stages
instances: Mac v0.63.0: committed + pushed, but dotprofile pull blocked (stage 4), hooks crashed (stage 5), deploy failed (stage 5), no verification (stage 6)
harvesting/ stale: produced (stage 1) but never committed (stage 2)
patterns.structuralFix: Each stage needs its own enforcement. Stage 1: OL-PR1 (auto-commit closes gap between produce and commit). Stage 4: D-v8-3 (dotprofile pre-pull mitigation). Stage 5: D-v8-4/D-v8-5 (hook portability, deploy script diagnostics). Stage 6: OL-PR5 (Lagebeurteilung at every transition). No single fix closes all 6 stages.
provenance: Swiss cheese model (Reason) — each stage is a layer with holes
Lean value stream mapping (waste at handoffs)

patterns.description: Operational learning is not a standalone artifact — it's a layer that attaches to every harness activity. Sessions, mission command, delegation, artifacts, frameworks, provenance, channels all produce and consume learning. Across all provenance (CALL institutional, Deming embedded, Argyris double-loop, SRE event-driven, safety engineering contextual): learning is embedded in the process, accumulated across events, and applied continuously. A separate OL file captures the SYNTHESIS but not the learning itself — the learning happens everywhere

proposals.proposal: Implement decision #1 (auto-commit/push) as the highest-priority pipeline fix. Every session without it loses harvested artifacts and session archives. The running estimate proved carry-forward works when committed — extend to all SessionEnd outputs
proposals.barrierAnalysis: If decision #1 had been implemented before session 5HyCwPtSDH: harvesting artifacts from 3/20-3/22 would be on Windows now. Session archives in dotprofile would be committed. The 'stale by 3 days' observation would not exist. PASSES barrier test

proposals.proposal: Add a hook portability check to the pre-commit check scripts. Grep all registered hooks for known-bad patterns (stat -f, find -printf, grep -P, date -d) and flag them. This is the missing detection layer
proposals.barrierAnalysis: If a portability check existed before the stop hooks were committed: the stat -f pattern would have been flagged. The hook would have been written with uname dispatch from the start. PASSES barrier test for OL-O2, OL-O3, OL-O7

proposals.proposal: Establish OL estimate as the cumulative institutional learning accumulator — separate from per-session running estimates, consuming AARs from across sessions. OL estimate grows; session estimates update in place. Both carry forward via git
proposals.barrierAnalysis: PENDING — depends on Mac-side AAR schema verification (CFG-A7). The OL estimate may need to consume or align with the AAR format developed on Mac. Analyze after Mac AARs are accessible.

proposals.proposal: Add Lagebeurteilung requirement at every execution transition — not just delegations and handoffs. When a commander decision authorizes execution, the agent must assess terrain before writing code: scope, approach, risks, dependencies on gapped state. The /delegate skill's delegation duty or a new standing order may be the natural home
proposals.barrierAnalysis: PENDING — the pattern (OL-P6) was observed once in this session. Per the escalation policy (decision #35): 1st occurrence = behavioral coaching, 3+ = structural fix. This is occurrence 1. Monitor for recurrence before investing in structural enforcement. However, the CALL provenance (PDCA Plan before Do, Lagebeurteilung every time) suggests structural enforcement is warranted even on first occurrence when the consequence is high (entire execution without commander checkpoint).

carryForwardGaps.description: Active intelligence requirements — state gaps that must be surfaced at lifecycle transition boundaries. Each gap states WHERE it's relevant, WHAT resolves it, and WHETHER it blocks specific execution. Consumed by: /handoff (include in handoff prompt), session start Lagebeurteilung (flag unresolved), lifecycle transition assessments (check dependencies). Adapted from IPB FM 2-01.3: intelligence gaps with collection plans, briefed at every operations order.
